name: Wall Sit

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: British Journal of Sports Medicine Isometric Tendon Protocol

steps: Stand with your back flat against a smooth wall, with your feet shoulder-width apart and roughly 2 feet out from the wall.
Slide your back down the wall until your thighs are nearly parallel to the floor and your knees are bent at roughly 90 degrees.
Ensure your knees are directly above your ankles, not extending past your toes.
Press your entire back and shoulders firmly into the wall and rest your hands on your hips or crossed over your chest.
Hold this isometric position for the desired duration while breathing calmly, then slide back up.
coaching_cues: Beginners can start at a higher angle (45 to 60 degrees) and gradually slide deeper as strength builds.
Do not rest your hands on your knees to support your weight.
Drive your heels down into the floor to keep tension distributed between quads and glutes.
